_note: The five facets (domain, layer, side, trust, use) for every served Knowledge page, keyed by page directory, back-filled 2026-11-04 by the knowledge facet audit; the schema and values are docs/design/THE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_STRUCTURE.md section 7, and the audit record is docs/staging/records/SEAT_RECORD_THE_KNOWLEDGE_FACET_AUDIT_2026-11-04.md.

insights.claim: Because the twelve-month limit runs from the demand for payment, not the bill or the read, a direct debit set too low can cost a supplier money even when every bill it sent was right.
insights.falsified_by: An Ofgem or Energy Ombudsman ruling that a correct bill, not a payment demand, starts the twelve-month clock for a direct-debit customer

insights.claim: The twelve-month limit protects a landlord of an ordinary let for a void period.
rests_on: our reading of the licence; Ofgem has not stated it
insights.falsified_by: An Ofgem statement, Ombudsman decision or court case holding a landlord liable beyond twelve months for a void

insights.claim: The simulated world's stock of debt more than 91 days old matched Ofgem's indicators when checked on 12 October 2026.
insights.falsified_by: A re-run whose 91-day debt stock falls outside Ofgem's published level

insights.claim: What drives a household to leave is a badly handled complaint, not dissatisfaction in general.
insights.falsified_by: A GB source showing dissatisfied non-complainants leave more than satisfied households, or no handling gradient once complaints about the switch itself are removed

insights.claim: Reputation acts as a durable stock: overcharging is penalised late.
insights.section: What this page does not yet establish
insights.falsified_by: A GB series showing customer losses from an overcharge ending within a year; the size and decay rate are unpublished, so only the shape is tested

insights.claim: Trust decides where a move goes more than whether a move happens.
insights.section: What this page does not yet establish
rests_on: Ofgem CIM waves 3-6 (distrusting households move supplier 1.2-1.6x; trusting ones change tariff with it 1.3-1.6x)
insights.falsified_by: A wave in which trust separates whether households move as strongly as where they go

insights.claim: A supplier's money in EV, solar and batteries comes from tariffs that move energy in time and from keeping the households that own the kit, much more than from energy volumes.
insights.falsified_by: Supplier accounts or a costed book in which volume margin on kit owners exceeds time-shift and retention value

insights.claim: Hedging is buying certainty, not trying to beat the market: a supplier accepts being worse off in falling markets as the price of surviving rising ones.
rests_on: source named only as 'standard energy trading practice'
insights.falsified_by: Published GB supplier accounts or Ofgem resilience reviews showing domestic hedge books run for trading profit rather than to lock the quoted margin

insights.claim: There is no optimal hedge the page can give, and a simulation that produced one would have optimised against its own history.
insights.falsified_by: A hedge rule that beats the layered mandate out of sample across 2016-2025 and a held-out market

insights.claim: For a gas-heated home the measures that save the most carbon, and most often money too, are heating measures, not changes to when electricity is used.
insights.falsified_by: Measured timing-shift carbon savings comparable with heating-measure savings at 2024-25 grid intensity, once the unverified inputs are replaced by sourced ones

insights.claim: A supplier's flexibility value now lies in automated, tariff-embedded shifting rather than paid events.
insights.falsified_by: Event payments recovering well above 2024/25 levels, or measured automated shifting worth less per home than paid events

insights.claim: Most households are on a standard variable tariff because of an absence of decisions, not because they chose it; choosing and paying are separated by years.
insights.falsified_by: Survey or trial evidence that a majority of default-tariff households actively chose the default over an available fix

insights.claim: The small minority who act each year act overwhelmingly on price.
insights.falsified_by: The page's own source: 'get a cheaper tariff' was 44% of switchers' reasons, under half; a larger base showing price below a majority would refute it

insights.claim: A supplier that cannot tell background change in a house from what it caused cannot honestly claim to have saved anyone anything.
rests_on: proving-and-showing-household-savings (uncontrolled studies find about 9.6% where controlled find about 2%)
insights.falsified_by: A savings estimate shown unbiased without a comparison group or a background-change model

insights.claim: In our model, over 2016-2025 on 3,000 homes, 10.6% of homes change insulation without their recorded energy rating changing.
insights.falsified_by: A re-measure on the current model giving a materially different share

insights.claim: Defect in our model: gas-heated homes eligible for a heat pump never reach boiler replacement, so 71% of homes have a boiler that can never be replaced.
insights.falsified_by: A run of the current model where those homes do reach boiler replacement

insights.claim: A synthetic book represents Britain when the distribution of what its households do matches, so a chosen-and-weighted sample beats a random one; on the full demand vector 8,823 to 11,522 households match a 120,000 reference within five points.
insights.falsified_by: A re-run of tools/demand_vector_coverage.py where a random sample of the same size passes, or where the figure keeps rising against a larger reference (the page itself says convergence is not shown)

insights.claim: The quantity to rank customers on is what an action changes, not how likely the customer is to leave; doing nothing is always an option.
insights.falsified_by: A GB trial in which targeting the highest-churn-propensity customers retains as many as targeting the highest uplift

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the weather-driven demand engine and the solar, battery and EV advice would transfer to Australia, while the price replay, settlement and billing would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the weather and wholesale price engines would transfer to Belgium, while billing, settlement and debt would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the demand engine and asset advice (after recalibration) would transfer to France, while tariffs, settlement and network limits would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the physics and price replay would transfer to Germany, while billing, tariff, settlement and debt machinery would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the weather engine and debt principles would transfer to Italy, while the connection model, zonal 15-minute prices, billing, default service and arrears rules would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the 30-minute clock and the meter-data feed would transfer to Japan, while heating, cooling, area prices, regulated tariff, billing and new-occupant rules would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Of the GB build, the weather engine would transfer to Spain, while the regulated dynamic price, power subscription, network tariff and billing would need rebuilding.
rests_on: the advisor's transferability ratings (judgement, not a measurement)
insights.falsified_by: A component-by-component port in which a component rated as transferring needs rebuilding, or one rated for rebuilding carries over

insights.claim: Most of what the GB build does to model households transfers to other markets, but most of the GB supplier's commercial rules (prepayment, the fixed direct debit, the all-supplier cap, supplier-owned meters, the deemed contract, the SoLR levy) are GB peculiarities.
rests_on: the seven country pages and research notes
insights.falsified_by: A second-market port in which household modelling needs rebuilding or the named GB rules turn out common elsewhere

insights.claim: Germany and Belgium are closest to GB, Japan furthest.
insights.section: What the data should look like
rests_on: the advisor's closeness ranking (judgement, not a measured distance)
insights.falsified_by: A measured distance over the sixteen dimensions that orders the countries differently

insights.claim: A household's needs split into cost, cash flow, certainty, control, time and carbon above a comfort and health floor, and different households feel each.
insights.falsified_by: Cross-tabs in which the same attribute separates every need equally, so the needs do not fall on different households

insights.claim: Difficulty paying bills, not income, separates who is hit by cost, cash-flow squeeze and worry.
insights.falsified_by: A later wave or a household-level dataset (e.g. Understanding Society) where income separates these measures as much as bill difficulty once age is held

insights.claim: Age separates who will switch supplier and who will pay more for green or service.
rests_on: CIM wave 3 stated intent (41.6% at 16-24, 9.0% at 75+)
insights.falsified_by: Already partly contested: the revealed age gap is +3 to +7 points against +19 to +32 stated and fading by 2025; refuted if it reaches zero

insights.claim: Trust in the supplier decides whether a price rise feels fair.
rests_on: CIM wave 3 (-30.3 points among distrusting households)
insights.falsified_by: A wave in which fairness of a rise does not differ by trust

insights.claim: Price sensitivity is two traits, cutting use and shopping around, not one dial.
insights.section: What this page does not yet establish
insights.falsified_by: Household-level data where cutting use and comparing tariffs move together with age and income

insights.claim: Worry about bills peaks at ages 35-54.
rests_on: advisor prediction written before the tables were read
insights.falsified_by: Refuted by CIM wave 3: worry is a plateau to 54, not a 35-54 peak

insights.claim: Income is a strong gradient for cost, cash-flow and worry needs.
rests_on: advisor prediction written before the tables were read
insights.falsified_by: Refuted by CIM wave 3: income separates far less than bill difficulty, its top-band gap not excluded from zero

insights.claim: Need is anti-correlated with switching: the most squeezed households switch less.
rests_on: advisor prediction written before the tables were read
insights.falsified_by: Refuted by CIM waves 3-6: households behind on bills state and report more switching (8.2-9.3% against 3.5-4.1%)

insights.claim: Control is lower when a household is behind on bills.
rests_on: sister page on payment method, wave 3 only
insights.falsified_by: Did not hold past wave 3; restated as "not higher"

insights.claim: In our simulated world, one measure that could not see a household's first year (the bill-shock count) produced the whole apparent link between tenure and loyalty.
insights.falsified_by: A run of the old measure with year one made visible in which the tenure gradient survives

insights.claim: A churn-by-tenure table is only as honest as the measures behind it in each year; a measure blind in some years can manufacture a pattern.
insights.falsified_by: Hard to refute as a method rule; refuted in a given table by showing every measure is defined in every year

insights.claim: Real GB evidence points the other way from the simulated gradient: new customers are less loyal than long-standing ones.
insights.falsified_by: Published GB data showing first-year customers retained at higher rates than long-tenure ones

insights.claim: A household choosing between a fix and its variable deal compares a real forward price with an implied one that nobody is offering, because both the cap headline and comparison sites annualise today's variable rate.
insights.falsified_by: Comparison sites or Ofgem headlines quoting a variable tariff on its expected forward path rather than today's rate held for a year

insights.claim: How finely Britain must be divided for pricing is a price list, not one number: 34, 89 or 987 weather cells depending on the tolerance, because household-weighted weather variation is far simpler than the terrain.
insights.section: A cell is a climate class, not a region
insights.falsified_by: A re-partition on the same sources where cell counts at the stated tolerances change materially, or household-weighted variation tracking terrain variation

insights.claim: A customer's value is contribution multiplied by survival, so the drivers are an order: does it pay, does it stay, how big is the margin bet, then everything else; for a negative-contribution customer churn is a benefit and loyalty-building is harmful.
insights.falsified_by: A variance decomposition of fully-costed value on a costed book where the drivers do not fall in that order

insights.claim: H1: bad debt and the cost to serve it dominate the downside of customer value.
insights.section: What the data should look like
insights.falsified_by: A variance decomposition putting debt and collections below 40% of downside variance

insights.claim: H4: value-add products earn through loyalty, not direct income.
insights.section: What the data should look like
insights.falsified_by: Measuring the loyalty parameter rather than assuming it

insights.claim: H5: accurate forecasting and billing is worth as much as value-add, possibly more.
insights.section: What the data should look like
insights.falsified_by: A supplier forecasting on premise physics showing no fall in churn, contacts, debt or volume risk

insights.claim: H6: the apathetic are the quiet engine and the right action is restraint.
insights.section: What the data should look like
insights.falsified_by: The disengaged archetype not ranking near the top on lifetime value, or unsolicited offers not raising their churn

insights.claim: H7: controllable assets with permission are the only large value-add upside, and solar alone is negative to the supplier.
insights.section: What the data should look like
insights.falsified_by: Measured shape value of a permissioned EV and battery outside £60-120 a year, or solar positive to the supplier

insights.claim: H9: smart metering pays through collectability, not through metering cost.
insights.section: What the data should look like
insights.falsified_by: Debt outcomes no better on smart than traditional meters at the same payment method

insights.claim: H10: a book drawn in population proportion averages £600-700 contribution before acquisition, netting to the market's ~£150 per customer.
insights.section: What the data should look like
rests_on: OVO/SSE 2020 (£143) and E.ON/OVO 2026 (~£150) transaction prices as reported
insights.falsified_by: A costed book that does not land near £150 after a buyer's overhead

insights.claim: Because house properties come in bundles, the homes where the potential to save is largest are a thin, specific minority that an average-home model never sees.
insights.falsified_by: A NEED-based decomposition showing saving potential spread evenly across the stock rather than concentrated

insights.claim: 233 deliberately chosen houses reproduce 99% of the household-weighted variation across five measured outputs of our model of British housing; one tail in five does not close.
insights.falsified_by: A re-measure on the current model giving a materially different count or coverage

insights.claim: Area deprivation adds little to energy use once the house itself is known.
insights.falsified_by: A NEED cross-tab where deprivation decile moves metered use materially within the same size, fabric and fuel band

insights.claim: Mileage follows the driver, not the fuel: high-mileage drivers choose diesel or electric cars rather than the fuel making people drive further, so a simulated home must draw its people and their mileage before its car.
insights.falsified_by: A panel showing a household's mileage rising after it switches to a cheaper-per-mile car, beyond what its prior mileage predicts

insights.claim: Occupancy has to be learned from the meter, not looked up from the address, because an output area explains only 9% of household size.
insights.falsified_by: A published or derived address-level predictor explaining well over 9% of household size, or meter data that cannot separate occupancy either

insights.claim: The simulated book's expected household size and payment-method risk figures, measured 27 Sep 2026; the book showing prepayment at 2.5 times direct debit reproduces its input and is not confirmation.
insights.falsified_by: A redraw of the book whose expected mean household size drifts well away from the national 2.359
